About Deriv

Deriv is bringing job-ready builders together in Dubai for a focused, high-signal hackathon experience designed to showcase real engineering ability in a real-world setting.


This event is built for experienced technical participants (primarily AI engineering, software engineering, data, and QA profiles) who thrive on problem-solving, teamwork, and shipping working prototypes under time pressure. High-potential final-year students and fresh graduates may be considered as an additional pipeline.

Top-performing participants will be shortlisted for interviews, with the objective of moving from hackathon to interview and hiring within 4–8 weeks. Participants must be professionally fluent in English.

Hackathon Details

Join lablab.ai hackathon and innovate using the latest models in the market. Discover all the relevant details below.

🦸🏼‍♂️ Who can join?

Job-ready technical professionals with 2–8 years of experience, as well as fresh graduates, in AI engineering, software engineering, data, or QA. Must be fluent in English.

🛠️ How to participate

Register on lablab.ai and join the lablab.ai Discord Server. Click "Sign up" at the bottom of this page and review our  Hackathon Guidelines and Getting Started Guide. The event runs hybrid: on-site in Business Bay, Dubai + online via lablab.ai.

😅 What if I don't have a team?

No problem. Find teammates on our dashboard or Discord server.

CHALLENGE

Build a job-ready AI prototype with a clear real-world use case

Your mission is simple: build and demo a real AI product prototype in a way that demonstrates strong execution, clear thinking, and team delivery.



What you need to deliver

  • By the end of the hackathon, your team should have:

    ✅ A working demo (something we can run and test)
    ✅ A clear problem statement (what you’re solving and for who)
    ✅ A solution flow (how the user interacts with it, end-to-end)
    ✅ Solid implementation (clean, maintainable code and sound architecture)
    ✅ A short presentation (what you built, how it works, why it matters)



    • What you can build

    Pick one direction and go deep. Examples include:

    • • AI workflow assistants (automation, internal tools, triage, knowledge support)

    • • Data & insights tools (dashboards, monitoring, anomaly detection, forecasting)

    • • QA & engineering automation (test generation, bug triage, regression detection)

    • • Risk / security / compliance support (alerts, auditing flows, policy enforcement)


        Choose at least one challenge track from the list below         and build AI solutions that solve real-world problems while pushing the boundaries of what’s possible!



How to begin

• Choose your challenge | Pick at least 1 challenge that excites you (you may choose more)

• Work solo or with your team | Be creative and exchange different ideas to choose the best one

• Questions? Contact us on lablab.ai Discord Server

  • Hackathon Free Resources Starter Pack

    1. Hosting & Backend (Free / Generous Free Tiers)

    Compute & APIs

    • Vercel
      Best for frontend + serverless APIs. Zero config, fast deploys, great for demos.

    • Netlify
      Similar to Vercel. Works well for static sites and simple functions.

    • Railway
      Easy backend hosting for Node, Python, Postgres, Redis.

    • Render
      Good for APIs, background jobs, and databases with free tiers.

    • Cloudflare Workers + Pages
      Excellent for edge APIs, auth gateways, and fast global demos.

    Databases

    • Supabase
      Postgres + Auth + Storage. Ideal for hackathons.

    • Neon
      Serverless Postgres with instant provisioning.

    • Firebase (Firestore + Auth)
      Great for real-time apps and fast prototyping.

    2. AI Models & LLM APIs (Free Credits / Free Usage)

    General LLMs

    • OpenAI (Chat Completions / Responses API)
      Usually comes with free credits for new accounts.

    • Google Gemini (Gemma Models)
      Generous free tier, good for reasoning and multimodal use cases.

    • Mistral AI
      Fast and open-friendly models with free tiers.

    Open Source Models

    • Hugging Face Inference API
      Access to thousands of models. Free tier available.

    • Ollama or LM Studio (Local LLMs)
      Run models like Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek locally.

    • Groq Cloud
      Ultra-fast inference with free access for supported models.

    LLM Frameworks

    • LangChain and LangGraph
      Industry giant for general-purpose development

    • Google ADK
      Designed to empower developers to quickly build, manage, evaluate and deploy AI-powered agents.

    Specialized AI

    • Whisper / Open-source ASR for speech-to-text (free when run locally)

    • Stable Diffusion (via Replicate or HF Spaces) for images

    • Sentence Transformers for embeddings and search

    3. Data Sources (Open, Safe, Hackathon-Friendly)

    General Open Data

    • Kaggle Datasets
      Finance, healthcare, fraud, NLP, user behavior.

    • Google Dataset Search

    • data.gov and data.europa.eu

    • World Bank Open Data

    • UN Data

    APIs for Demos

    • OpenWeather API

    • NewsAPI

    • Alpha Vantage (finance)

    • CoinGecko (crypto market data)

    • OpenStreetMap APIs

    Synthetic Data

    • Mockaroo
      Generate realistic fake datasets.

    • Faker libraries https://github.com/joke2k/faker
      Create users, transactions, logs, events.

    • Synthea (healthcare synthetic data)

    No real PII or production data should be used.


    4. UI / UX / Design Tools (Free Plans)

    Design & Prototyping

    • Figma
      Wireframes, UI kits, collaborative design.

    • Penpot
      Open-source alternative to Figma.

    • Canva
      Pitch decks, landing pages, quick visuals.

    • Google AI studio
      Google AI Studio is a build-first tool for developing application logic and functional code.

    • Google Stitch
      Google Stitch is a design-first tool for creating visuals and user interfaces (UI).

    UI Components

    • 21st.dev (https://21st.dev/community)

    • Quill V2 (https://deriv-com.github.io/quill-v2/?section=buttons), https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deriv-com/quill-v2-cli?activeTab=readme)

    • Shadcn UI (https://ui.shadcn.com/)

    • MUI

    • Chakra UI

    • Ant Design

    • Tailwind CSS (https://tailwindcss.com/)

    Icons & Assets

    • Heroicons

    • Lucide Icons

    • Phosphor Icons

    • Unsplash / Pexels for images

    5. Low-Code / No-Code (Optional but Allowed)

    • Bubble

    • Retool (free tier)

    • Xano

    • Appsmith

    • n8n for workflows and automations

    Must clearly show where AI logic lives and how it adds value.

    6. Auth, Identity & Integrations

    • Clerk.dev

    • Auth0 (free tier)

    • Supabase Auth

    • Firebase Auth

    Integrations

    • Slack APIs

    • Discord Bots

    • Email APIs (Resend, SendGrid free tier)

    • Webhooks

    7. Collaboration & Dev Tools

    • GitHub for code hosting

    • GitHub Actions for CI

    • Postman / Hoppscotch for API testing

    • VS Code

    • Cursor / Continue.dev for AI-assisted coding

    • https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code

    8. Demo & Presentation

    • Loom for demo recordings

    • Google Slides / Canva for pitch decks

    • OBS if doing live demos

    • Mermaid.js for architecture diagrams

    9. Guardrails & Expectations

    • Use only public, open, or synthetic data

    • No scraping behind logins or paywalls

    • No production credentials or real user data

    • AI must be core to the solution, not a wrapper

    • Code should be deployable or runnable locally

    10. Suggested “Golden Path” Stack (If Teams Are Stuck)

    • Frontend: Next.js + Tailwind

    • Backend: Vercel or Railway

    • DB: Supabase

    • AI: OpenAI or Gemini

    • Design: Figma

    • Data: Kaggle or Mockaroo

Judging Criteria
Application of Technology
How effectively the chosen model(s) are integrated into the solution.
Presentation
The clarity and effectiveness of the project presentation.
Business Value
The impact and practical value, considering how well it fits into business areas.
Originality
The uniqueness & creativity of the solution, highlighting approaches and ability to demonstrate  behaviors.

What to submit?

📋 Basic Information

• Project Title

• Short Description

• Long Description

• Technology & Category Tags

📸 Cover Image and Presentation

• Cover Image

• Video Presentation

• Slide Presentation

💻 App Hosting & Code Repository

• Public GitHub Repository

• Demo Application Platform

• Application URL

For further details and guidance, please visit Submission Guidelines
